title: Token-stream stability microbench with adaptive warmup and sliding-window p95 detector
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build and maintain a tokens-per-second microbenchmark focused on steady-state token throughput stability (not just peak TPS). The suite should detect small regressions in p95 token latency and sustained token/sec across model variants and kernel/quantization changes. This ticket covers harness design, CI integration, dashboarding, and the first three model profiles (gpt-like-7B, llama-13B, rw-13B-INT8).
background: Existing TPS suites measure peak throughput and stepped-load behavior, but we have recurring flakiness when kernel changes or warmup heuristics are introduced. Teams need an automated stability detector that tolerates short transient jitter but catches persistent regressions (e.g., >3% sustained drop in tokens/sec or >10ms p95 regression across 5 consecutive CI runs).
approach_and_design: Create a token-stream generator that simulates realistic chat-like request sizes (mix of 8-64 token user prompts with 64-512 token responses) and adheres to per-second arrival jitter to surface scheduling pathologies.
Adaptive warmup: before measuring steady-state, run incremental warmup passes where batch sizes and KV cache states are primed; warmup length learned per-model via a short calibration step (90s max).

Sliding-window stability metrics: compute tokens/sec and p95 over overlapping 60s windows with a 30s step, then compute a run-level stability score (median tokens/sec, 95th percentile of p95 samples).

Noise-aware regression detector: store rolling historical baseline (30 most recent CI results); flag regression when median tokens/sec drops by >=3% and run-level p95 increases by >=10ms with statistical significance (bootstrap p < 0.05) across 3 consecutive runs.
KV-cache and prefix awareness: harness will support empty-cache and primed-cache modes and report both to surface regressions that only affect cache handling.

Profile artifacts: produce a per-run JSON artifact with time-series of tokens emitted, per-request latency, batch utilization, GPU occupancy sampled from the runtime, and kernel selection logs to help triage.
CI integration: run lightweight suite on PRs affecting runtime/compilation code (fast profile, ~6m) and full stability suite nightly (full profile, ~45m).
Alerting & dashboard: add Grafana panel and synthetic alert (PagerDuty/Slack) if regression detector trips or if nightly variance exceeds threshold.
Acceptance criteria listed below must be met before marking Done.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible harness repository under infra/benchmarks/token_stream with README and example configs for the three initial models.
CI job definitions accepted in .buildkite and gated on runtime-impacting PRs.
Regression detector implemented and validated on historical CI traces (run on last 120 CI runs and correctly report historical regression events introduced by ENG-11024 changes).
Per-run JSON artifact emitted to build artifacts and ingested into observability pipeline (Grafana/Elastic) with dashboards showing median tokens/sec, sliding-window p95, and stability score.
Runbook created describing triage steps, common failure modes, and links to kernel-selection logs and example PR labels to block merges automatically when P0 regressions are detected.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: GPU cluster time for nightly suite grows as we add more models. Mitigation: cap nightly to top-5 customer-impact models and run lower-priority models weekly.
Risk: High false-positive rate from noisy environments. Mitigation: use sliding-window + bootstrap test and require consecutive run detection before paging.
Risk: Artifacts are large (GPU counters, kernel traces). Mitigation: compress and sample traces; keep full traces for 30 days only.
Risk: Runtime changes that alter measurement semantics. Mitigation: add metadata to artifacts indicating runtime version, kernel flags, and hardware IDs so baselines are comparable.
